title: Recording VAT margin scheme transactions
text:
Records to keep

 You must keep normal VAT records (section 19 of VAT Notice 700)  when you use the margin scheme. However, there are some specific records to keep for the margin scheme .

 If you don’t make a profit on a sale of margin scheme goods

 If your purchase price is higher than, or the same as, your selling price then there is no margin so no VAT will be due. In these circumstances you should show the margin and the VAT due as ‘nil’ in your stock book.

 Changing a VAT margin scheme transaction

 Re-invoicing outside of a margin scheme

 If you’ve sold goods and the buyer later decides that they wish to treat the transaction outside the scheme, you may re-invoice for the goods under the normal VAT rules, provided that:

 • you’re able to comply with the relevant VAT regulations for the substitute transaction

 • at the time of the amendment, you and the buyer hold the original records for the transaction

 If you’re willing to re-invoice, you must cancel the first entry in your records and cross-refer to the amended transaction.

 The replacement invoice must show:

 • the original transaction and advise that it’s cancelled

 • that the buyer should amend their VAT account

 Find out more about  how to correct VAT errors and make adjustments or claims .

 Re-invoicing under the margin scheme

 If you’ve sold goods that were eligible for sale under a margin scheme outside of a margin scheme, you cannot subsequently treat the supply as a margin scheme supply.

 Further information

 You must show any goods you buy or sell using a margin scheme on  your VAT return .

 Tertiary legislation

 You can find the legal conditions in VAT tertiary legislation :

 • Section 2 – stock book requirements

 • Section 3 – stock number

 • Section 4 – sales invoice requirements

 • Section 5 – self-billed invoices requirements

 • Section 6 – global accounting

 • Section 7 – pawned goods

 • Section 8 – occasional sales

 • Section 9 – sale or return

 High value goods sold for cash

 Accepting cash payments for second-hand goods you sell will not affect your margin scheme calculations. However, if you sell goods for the equivalent of 10,000 euros or more, and take payment for it in cash, you will need to register with HMRC as a  high value dealer .
